# Files, audio, and browser

[Documentation](README.md) · [Project overview](../README.md)

> This guide retains the detailed reference material from the original README.
> Dated acceptance reports describe past checks, not a current deployment or test result.

## Chat attachments

### Files generated by Moyai

After a workspace save, **Files** opens a searchable list with Markdown/text
previews and individual downloads. Saved filenames in assistant replies and
public updates are clickable, including existing messages such as
`Created **design.md**` and links to `/workspace/design.md`. Exact workspace paths
take precedence; a bare filename only resolves to a nested file when unambiguous.

Explicitly published files have immutable, verified revisions and complete
downloads, without starting a sandbox. Text previews load further ranges on
request. The recovery ZIP also preserves full collected files and tracked edits;
files omitted by an older collector cannot be reconstructed from its archive.
All routes require the session's organization sign-in. HTML/scripts stay inert.
A replaced recovery archive requests a refresh rather than silently serving
different bytes; explicit artifact revisions remain independently readable.

### Files uploaded by users

Attach files with the paperclip, drag/drop, or paste. Both new sessions and
follow-ups show removable previews before sending. Moyai retains every selected
file and its complete bytes; there is no per-message file count, per-file size,
or message-total ceiling. The administrator's workspace storage budget still
applies. If storage is full, remove unsent drafts or ask the administrator to
increase `ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_LIMIT_MB` with enough backing capacity.

Uploads use session-bound encrypted parts. An interrupted upload keeps its
acknowledged parts; **Retry** verifies those same parts and completes the file
without creating another attachment. The server checks sign-in, origin, CSRF,
upload identity and part contents before publication. A partially uploaded file
cannot be sent to an agent. Older browser tabs retain the single-request route;
refresh the page to use complete multipart uploads.

Raster images have sanitized previews; text documents show a labeled excerpt.
Originals remain available even when a decoder or transcription provider cannot
process them. The file card reports that processing failure, and the agent is
told to inspect the retained original before making claims about it. Preview
work remains bounded separately from original-file retention: PNG, JPEG, WebP
and GIF previews accept up to 25 megapixels and use the first GIF frame.

Drafts are private to their uploader. Sending binds each file to the exact
message in the same transaction as admission, with the session's existing
access rules. Unsent drafts expire after 24 hours on a later upload. Complete
parts and previews use the configured database or private object storage; see
[object storage](object-storage.md) for migration and verification. The default
workspace attachment budget is 256 MiB and is configurable. Downloads require
authentication and serve originals as attachments; only decoded previews render
inline.

Each active turn restores its sent files under
`/workspace/.moyai-attachments/<id>/<filename>`, streaming to a temporary file
and verifying the complete size and hash before replacement. Later queued
messages' files remain unavailable until that turn is admitted. Referenced image
previews are added once per model request without a ten-image selection cutoff.
The chosen model's actual input/media capacity still applies; originals remain
available as files. File contents are reference data and do not grant authority
or install a skill automatically.

Web messages mirrored to Slack include attachment names and a protected session
link. These uploaded originals remain in Moyai. Agent output captures use the
separate [native Slack delivery](slack.md#chat-with-moyai-in-slack) path.

Incoming Slack files use the same durable parts and inspection pipeline. Signed
mentions, direct messages and bound-thread replies retain every valid file ID,
including image-only messages. AgentChat normalizes references in batches. Moyai
then resolves live `files.info` access and streams from Slack's private file host
with the bot's `files:read` credential, without following redirects or passing
private URLs/tokens to the model. Metadata size is verified against received
bytes. The live API response determines access, since saved scopes may be stale.
A missing scope asks the user to reconnect Slack; other failures report the
actual missing input without guessing its contents.

Initial context can recover files absent from an `app_mention` and files in the
explicitly invoked thread. Nearby channel files and future queued replies are
excluded. Direct-message history is not imported. Connection-policy and team
checks run before download, after inspection and before binding. Downloads and
transcription stay off the webhook acknowledgment path. The durable intake table
retains its legacy `slack_audio_inputs` name for compatibility.

## Audio input

Moyai accepts Slack voice clips and uploaded MP3, WAV, M4A/MP4, WebM, OGG and FLAC files. In the web composer, use **Record audio** or attach/drop a recording, wait for **Transcript ready**, then open the attachment to review the transcript and play the original. **Edit in message** copies an uploaded transcript into the composer; microphone recordings insert their transcript automatically. Correct the text before sending. Explicit message text takes precedence over the original transcript. Audio-only messages are valid. Browser recording requires HTTPS (or localhost), microphone permission and a supported MediaRecorder implementation; recording continues until you stop or cancel it. Navigating away or locking the composer releases the microphone. Browser and provider resource constraints still apply.

Optional `AUDIO_TRANSCRIPTION_PROMPT` supplies a short spelling glossary without sending prior conversation history. Transcription uses `POST /audio/transcriptions` on `LITELLM_API_BASE`, authenticated with the existing server-side `LITELLM_API_KEY`. Set `AUDIO_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` to a transcription model/alias enabled for that gateway key (default `gpt-transcribe`; `whisper-1` remains compatible when configured). Transcription is a model request and can incur provider charges, including when previewing an unsent draft. It also runs for audio uploaded in demo mode; demo **agent responses** remain simulated. No new provider key is exposed to the browser or agent sandbox.

Reconnect the Slack app once to grant its added `files:read` bot permission. Signed, authorized mentions, DMs and bound-thread replies retain the file IDs with the accepted message. The worker downloads only from Slack's private file host using the bot credential, transcribes outside the webhook acknowledgment, and attaches the original plus transcript to that sender's turn. Audio queued during a response takes a turn boundary before it is read. Download failures report missing content. A transcription failure preserves the original and reports that no transcript is available. Prior messages' unrelated Slack attachments are not backfilled.

Transcripts are automatic and may contain errors. They are stored alongside the original attachment and become part of the shared session when sent, with the same access rules as other user input. Drafts remain private to their uploader. Transcripts retain their complete returned text and can be copied into the composer without a character cutoff. Uploads/downloads use bounded transport parts; storage budgets, provider capabilities, concurrency and network timeouts remain explicit operational constraints. Audio playback streams verified byte ranges. File redirects are not followed.

To verify locally, configure a working transcription endpoint and run `uv run uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787`. Open the web composer, attach a short spoken request without typing text, preview its transcript, and send it. With the Slack permission installed, mention the bot with a voice clip and follow up with a second clip in that thread. Tests: `uv run pytest tests/test_audio.py tests/test_attachments.py tests/test_slack.py tests/test_slack_chat.py tests/test_message_queue.py` and `node --test tests/*.cjs`.

The input design follows the documented dictation pattern used by [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation), [Codex desktop dictation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/prompting#use-voice-dictation), [Cursor](https://prod.cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting#voice-input), and [Aider](https://aider.chat/docs/usage/voice.html): speech becomes text for the existing agent. [Aider's public implementation](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/voice.py#L169) uses LiteLLM transcription. Moyai uses the same provider-neutral API pattern, implemented here without copying their source. OpenAI currently recommends `gpt-transcribe` for [new file-transcription integrations](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/speech-to-text). Live spoken conversation, as offered by [Codex Voice](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/features/voice), is a separate capability from accepting recordings and is outside this change.

## Computer desktop and captures

The opt-in [independent runtime](independent-runtime.md) can answer connected-app
questions before starting the computer. Computer tools and **Wake up to see
live** acquire the workspace under the same turn.

The agent's `browser_read` exposes the full text and control directory of one
observed frame, including open shadow roots. It also lists frames for explicit
reads. Optional text and element ranges refer to a saved `snapshot`, so later
reads cannot silently combine different live page revisions. There is no fixed
24,000-character or 80-control cutoff. Closed components, canvas and image
contents still require visual inspection; lazy content may require scrolling.

Observed `target` references bind to exact DOM nodes. A replaced or changed node
rejects the action and requires a fresh read. Role/name and label selectors remain
available, as do screenshot coordinates, ordinary navigation, keyboard input,
horizontal/vertical scrolling, tab listing/selection, form selects, workspace-file
uploads, and completed downloads. Snapshot/target handles belong to the live
computer; after recovery, read a fresh observation before acting. Downloads return
their exact local path and size. Upload paths must remain within the workspace.
`browser_screenshot` supplies an image content block to the model as well as the
saved PNG path, allowing visual inspection on runtimes/models that support images.

Open **Computer** in a cloud session to use its Linux desktop and Chromium browser. **Take control** lets the requester or an administrator click and type directly into the desktop, including Chrome’s address bar and sign-in fields. Use Cmd/Ctrl+L for the address bar, paste from your clipboard, drag, scroll, or open tabs normally. Ctrl+Alt+Esc moves keyboard focus back to Moyai’s controls. **Open browser** reopens Chrome if you close its windows. Agent browser actions wait while a person holds control and resume on the selected tab when control is released. Closing the panel releases control, and an abandoned lease expires after 60 seconds. Human interaction refreshes the existing five-minute idle window, without extending the sandbox's absolute lifetime. **Wake up to see live** starts an asleep workspace from its last saved checkpoint without sending a chat message or running the model. It shows progress until the live desktop is ready; **Take control** remains a separate action. Wake uses the durable session runtime (enabled on the hosted deployment), shared sandbox capacity, and normal idle cleanup. If automatic post-response retention is disabled, an explicitly awakened computer still has a five-minute idle window. Legacy deployments must enable durable sessions to use this button. Manual desktop changes are retained while the machine is live; waking after shutdown restores the last saved checkpoint.

Coding tasks that create a PR default to running the changed behavior, recording a short real browser flow, and saving a useful screenshot, unless the user opts out. The final handoff includes the confirmed PR link, exact saved capture links, and what was verified. Documentation/backend changes without a meaningful browser flow use applicable checks; unavailable demos or captures are reported explicitly. This is agent guidance, not a guarantee that every task produces media, and it does not authorize public deployment.

You can also ask Moyai to take a screenshot or record a browser flow. Its MCP tools include `browser_screenshot`, `browser_record_start`, and `browser_record_stop`. The web panel has the same capture controls. Completed captures appear in a separate **Saved captures** workspace tab, with image previews, video playback, and individual downloads. Opening **Computer** adds **Saved captures** beside it; the **+** tab menu and **Saved captures** button also open the gallery. The gallery refreshes while visible and is also available through **Files** after the workspace closes. Switching tabs releases input control without stopping an active recording; return to its Computer or pull request tab to take control and stop it. Captures share the session's saved-file visibility. The live screen and controls are restricted to its requester or an administrator.

- Full-desktop PNG screenshots and WebM video, 1280 × 720, no audio.
- Each clip stops at 10 minutes or roughly 25 MB; 64 MB of saved captures per session.
- Recordings finish before a response checkpoint or idle sandbox shutdown. Incomplete files remain `.partial` and are never offered as finished videos.
- Completed captures are copied to the app's persistent disk, separately from code ZIPs, and included in optional cloud checkpoints. Existing downloads do not need a running sandbox.
- The desktop runs on Xvfb inside the session’s Modal or Substrate sandbox. Modal reuses a private exec connection for input and frames; Substrate uses its existing signed guest transport. Neither starts an interpreter per keystroke, and no public desktop, VNC, or debugging port is exposed. Idle connections expire and close on app shutdown. Restored older workspaces install missing desktop dependencies on first use. Running workspaces must restart to load the updated Computer service and Substrate guest route.

The main browser saves its cookies, local storage, IndexedDB, per-tab session storage and HTTP(S) tabs to an encrypted checkpoint for this session. It saves when control is released, at response completion and before graceful sandbox shutdown, including idle expiry; an open Computer panel also saves at most once every ten seconds. Waking the computer or starting the next response restores that checkpoint. New sessions and child agents have separate browser access, and PR review tabs are excluded. Browser checkpoints stay outside workspace files and are removed when the session is deleted. Website expiry or logout can still require another sign-in. An abrupt machine loss restores only the last completed checkpoint, and an already-running older Computer service needs a restart to gain this behavior.

Input is queued in order, and the view requests a new frame every 100 ms after a response while you have control (once per second when watching). Network latency and rendering still affect visible response time. After a connection error, check the desktop before resuming control; uncertain input is not automatically replayed. Pasted clipboard data is cleared when control ends. Do not record secrets or credentials.

If saved browser access cannot be read, Moyai preserves the checkpoint and reports the problem. Agent work that does not require the browser can continue; opening the affected Computer remains blocked until saved access can be restored.

Up to 32 tabs resume, including the active tab. A failed per-tab session storage read does not prevent saving healthy tabs and browser access; unavailable tab data uses its last saved value when the same tab has not navigated. Moyai reports partial saves. A failure to read the browser's cookies and site storage preserves the previous checkpoint. Browser access gets a bounded save attempt before recording cleanup during shutdown.


## Review pull requests beside the conversation

Open a session pull request from the conversation, the PR list, or a saved PR tab to see its status, branches, description, and changed-file diffs directly in Moyai. This read-only view uses the organization’s selected GitHub repositories and works while the cloud workspace is asleep. Refresh updates the details; Open in GitHub provides the full review, discussion, and checks interface.

The panel includes the session’s confirmed PRs and those of its child agents. Disabled GitHub access or removed repository selection makes the details unavailable. **Load more files** retrieves additional changed files and retains loaded pages when you return to the tab. Descriptions and provider-supplied patches remain complete. If the PR changes between pages, refresh before continuing. GitHub can omit patches or stop returning files; the panel reports those gaps. Computer and Saved captures retain their separate controls.

For a local demo, run `uv run python scripts/pull_request_panel_demo.py --port 8987` and open `http://localhost:8987/demo/login`. The session and GitHub data are fixtures. Add `--live-github` to read real PR details using your existing local `gh` login; no model, cloud workspace, or GitHub write is used.

## File and terminal tools

The shared computer tools read complete files in byte pages and return exact
base64 bytes, including binary files and UTF-8 characters split across pages.
`computer_write_file` publishes a complete replacement atomically; replacing an
existing file requires `overwrite=true` and preserves its executable mode.

`computer_terminal` returns a process handle. Commands continue after the tool
returns; use `computer_terminal_read` to inspect status and page through the full
saved output. A stable `request_key` identifies one launch across acknowledgment
retries. An unavailable supervisor has an unknown outcome and does not authorize
relaunching the command.

Use `computer_terminal_input` to send text, exact base64 bytes, EOF, or an explicit
force stop. When the process cannot accept all input immediately, the receipt
identifies the accepted prefix and returns the exact remaining base64 suffix.
Only send that remaining suffix again. Run services as foreground commands with
handles; descendants stop when their owning command exits. Logs and command
arguments stay outside repository trees, under the saved session directory.
